reviews.text: There are a few clichéd ghost motifs in this haunted house horror, but it's supremely watchable thanks to Rebecca Hall's exploration of a woman paralysed by grief.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: The Night House does not rely on traditional tropes or tactics to get a scare out of its viewers. It’s a slow, tense, admirably restrained burn that digs itself underneath your skin little by little.
reviews.author: Joseph Tomastik

reviews.text: A creepy, tension filled, dark descent that gets darker and darker the more you dive into the story. Rebecca Hall gives one of her best performances & David Bruckner directs the hell out of this
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: What's more terrifying — to have someone you love abruptly snatched away from you? Or to discover you're safer with them gone? Both revelations are crushing, and the film does a fine job laying the groundwork and leaving viewers to decide for themselves.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: The film works best when it is a straight up haunted house movie. When the third act takes a violent swerve into psychological thriller, What Lies Beneath-territory... the rock-solid performance of Hall will keep you invested.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: A film about picking up the pieces after your life has been completely shattered, The Night House is horror that cuts to the very soul through a devastating performance by Rebecca Hall.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: A warning to all who enter The Night House: this isn’t the film to watch before bed.
reviews.author: Mitchell Beaupre

reviews.text: Director David Bruckner's spine-tingling horror film is a chilling meditation on grief and depression that never gives easy answers to these questions.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: The Night House might not stick the landing, but it's an eerie supernatural chiller with an incredible lead performance from Rebecca Hall.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: Note to Ari Aster: this is how you make a horror movie about depression and suicidal ideation.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: The Night House creates an immersive and spooky mood that works in spite of some dissatisfying explanations in the last third.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Night House is emotionally intelligent, sufficiently unnerving, and thoroughly eerie.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: The idea that Hall should be the lead of more movies isn't new, but The Night House solidifies it as objective fact.
reviews.author: Vinnie Mancuso

reviews.text: The Night House is lucky to have Rebecca Hall.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: It's a rare treat as an adult horror fan to be properly scared in a film and The Night House gave me that sweet, sweet high, making my blood run cold more than once.
reviews.author: Daniel Rutledge

reviews.text: It's directed with elegance and delves into psychological horror. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: The Night House is the quickest way to spend nearly two hours, maintaining maximum tension and dread from minute one.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: This rather simple story is bent into a pretzel by Bruckner.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: ... The Night House takes the cognitive confusion of loss and grief and gives it a thriller spin, creating a tale that will have you question what it is you see and wondering what you don't see, even as you recline in a place of comfort.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: A restless exercise that never really gets under the skin but gets us minimally interested throughout.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Well directed and with a remarkable performance by Rebeca Hall. Not even the inconsistent ending manages to sink the film.
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: A masterful and spine-chilling supernatural thriller commanded by one of Rebecca Hall's best performances. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: A must watch for any horror fan, The Night House is a bone-chilling psychological thriller that will make your skin crawl.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: It might not be pure art, but "The Night House" does work, even if it's more on a dramatic level, than as a horror thriller. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Visually, audibly, and thematically, The Night House is an assaulting film, but because it works best in the gray areas between certainty and hysteria, the filling of the void, as it were, is a bit of a letdown.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: This could have easily been a movie of perpetual gaslighting, where friends gang up on the widow to force a devastating and finite reaction, but The Night House Doesn't play those cards.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: The best thing about The Dark House is that as it progresses, the entanglements get more and better. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall does a very, very good job, and this is genuinely scary.
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall does fine work in this psychological horror thriller that satisfies with an intelligent story and enough thrills. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: A lot of things are scary, but nothing's quite as scary as recent grief. That's the takeaway from this psychological horror film that mostly delivers
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: The first clever move The Night House makes is recognising it's floating into busy spectral waters, then ensuring its tension stems from its living, breathing protagonist as much as the frights and fears she's forced to face.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: In the realm of horror movies, The Night House might be unconventional, but it's no less powerful, atmospheric, or beautifully acted.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Clever framing, smart lighting and pitch perfect pacing means that, while the tension builds from the opening frames, when it finally reaches a crescendo, the results are chillingly effective.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: It's like the horror movie equivalent of the AutoTune fake-out in Brandon Flowers' "Lonely Town," and it's a major achievement to take a film so close along that precipice and still stick the landing.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: "The Night House" doesn't feel like it's solely relying on a familiar blueprint, and a lot of that is thanks to Hall's performance.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: On its surface, it's a chilling, mysterious ghost story, and you can absolutely enjoy it just as that ( ... ) But the film is also a dark exploration of relationships, mortality, loneliness, and grief.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Hall does tremendous work with the film, imbuing Beth not just with the traditional grief and anger one would feel in such a situation, but with a wry sense of humor and a cynical edge that can't help but be chipped away.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: The Night House, like its subjects, exists impossibly in two spaces at once, and our uneasiness blossoms from our inability to distinguish which side of the mirror we're on, even once it's over.
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Hall makes Beth, a woman forced to draw on inner reserves when faced with sinister forces, a compelling, relatable presence.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Confidently directed by David Bruckner from a clever script written by Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski, "The Night House" excels in tension building -it is both unpredictable and unnervingly restrained.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall carries this spooky film on her talented shoulders.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The filmmaker puts a formidable visual game of mirrors into practice, which fits beautifully with the story's unsettling conclusion. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall once again proves herself worthy of all the praise in this moody, atmospheric chiller.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: Hall carries this film effortlessly. Loved the horror elements mixed with the supernatural and the exploration of grief.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: From walls, pillars, glass, and shelves, they will forever be suspicious. The Night House instills that level of paranoia.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: ...a seriously misguided and misbegotten endeavor.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: There are times in which Bruckner's direction is too intellectual and not visceral enough.
reviews.author: Phil Guie

reviews.text: What does watching paint dry and watching grass grow have in common? They're more interesting than this movie. There's really nothing worse than a dull horror movie.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: The Night House is a genuinely creepy immersion driven by a writhing sense of dread and the tease of mystery.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Other than a richly textured performance by Rebecca Hall, this metaphysical haunted-house thriller doesn't do much to elevate itself above genre conventions.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Each new revelation and glimpse of terrifying truth is elegantly executed - most notably in an utterly chilling five minutes of ghost train chaos.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: The Night House has the gift of a very strong lead performance from Hall.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: As a gripping exploration of how grief can twist our clearest perceptions, it's a thrilling row across the waters of marital terror.
reviews.author: Eileen G'Sell

reviews.text: The Night House has a lot going for it, even it turns out to be another film where the filmmakers didn't think about whether the payoff worked before it was too late.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Often sardonic but finding strength in her character's vulnerability, Hall provides a captivating, grounded lead performance, ensuring that this tense and layered horror movie rings with real emotional resonance.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: David Bruckner [supplies] some of the best jump scares and blocking set-ups I've seen in a while. [But] the most memorable pieces ultimately outweigh the whole.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: A meticulously crafted haunted house story but one that falls short of paranormal perfection after a finale that feels built from the blueprints of something less daring and distinctive than its previous two acts.
reviews.author: Jonathan DeHaan

reviews.text: Bruckner's sophomore features Rebecca Hall in a powerhouse performance about the grief and anger that resides in the wake of a monumental personal loss.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: Rarely have I seen a movie in which simply everything demands clarification.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Hall ties herself into pretzel-like knots: flying high one moment, wallowing in self-pity and despair a nanosecond later.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Moody and atmospheric, sometimes to a fault, The Night House still delivers enough mystery and intrigue to make it a noteworthy psychological/supernatural horror movie. Rebecca Hall's effective performance improves the quality.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Intelligent, emotionally compelling and visually sophisticated, for fans of darker fare and old-fashioned spooky stories, The Night House is unmissable.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: Hall's Beth is no "scream queen" - the actor conveys the fear that builds in Beth as she uncovers Owen's dark secrets, but that fear motivates her to action rather than paralyzes her.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The Night House is a compelling meditation on the horror of one's own mind.
reviews.author: Becca James

reviews.text: The Night House may not be a horror masterpiece, but it is a masterpiece of manipulation, one in which we may not always understand what's going on...
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: The Night House is a strong argument for more films that let Rebecca Hall be a scream queen.
reviews.author: Cody Corrall

reviews.text: The Night House is pretty good, but it galls to know that it is so very nearly great.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: 'The Night House' could have settled just to be a haunted house story, but Rebecca Hall's performance shows how hard it is navigate grief alone with secrets to bare.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Hall is the actor you want for this assignment... The British star has a default setting of keen, sturdy credibility that makes fear and self-disbelief all the more intrusive and alarming.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: Once more of the mystery and terror escalates in the film, Hall is a suitable anchor to lock audiences in for the emotional ride.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: It's skillfully executed enough to make The Night House worth a look on technical merit alone, turning every corner of a luxurious lake house into a site of deep dread.
reviews.author: Keith Phipps

reviews.text: For all the overtones of the supernatural, it is the terror of slipping into very real madness that drives it, making it a first-rate psychological thriller that will leave you shaken to your core.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: With a bit of It Follows, a dash of The Babadook, and a hint of The Entity, herein lies a thriller that dares to personify depression itself, giving form to concept that isn't just a metaphor.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: "...manages to both refresh some of horror's most frequently revisited tropes and deliver a whopping dose of tension at the same time, all anchored by an astonishing central performance from Rebecca Hall."
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: David Bruckner's The Night House is undeniably one of the freshest, chilling, and human psychological horror thrillers I've seen in quite some time.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: With a fine performance from Hall, the opening hour is terrific. The dénouement, however, will be divisive.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The fuzzy plotting is balanced by Hall's brilliantly controlled performance as the caustic, sceptical Beth, whose grief has pushed her to the knife edge of sanity.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Hall carries every scene and keeps us guessing all the way. She plays this woman's nerves like a Stradivarius.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: The Night House is a solid piece of horror featuring plenty of atmosphere and a compelling lead performance, but it doesn't quite stick the landing when it comes to its ending.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: ...when you give an incredibly talented actress the opportunity they can spur you alongside quality direction into a deeply emotional experience of thrills and chills...
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: [David] Bruckner's existential terror exercise is one I truly implore all audiences to check in to.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: While it doesn't totally click in every way, David Bruckner's chiller still manages some truly mind-bending, soul-shuddering scares, which work largely because of Hall's wrenching performance.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Right from the earliest images, the reason to take any of it seriously becomes the versatile Hall, showing off a remarkable mix of sorrow, terror, toughness and turmoil. Award possiblities anyone?
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A thrilling Ride
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Even if you end up frustrated at the plot being vague, you will acknowledge the film's power in keeping you disturbed and never letting go of its grip.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: "The Night House" commits the cardinal sin for a horror movie: It's dull.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: I will never look at the shadows in my bedroom the same way again. Thank you for ruining my life,  The Night House.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: With many gasp-worthy moments throughout, it's a horror film of the best kind - one that brings its own genius while playing with familiar staples and tropes.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: Without Rebecca Hall, this would have been a fizzle, but she makes it come alive, and she is why you'll want to see this movie.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: It never really comes to fruition and I felt frustrated by the end.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Disappointing, but it is kind of effective and diverting.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: It's an immensely satisfying horror thriller that fully embraces its genre elements while also shrewdly dealing with some heavy topics such as mortality, depression, grief and suicide.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Hall's stellar performance can only do so much, especially when familiar horror tropes quickly start to spread throughout the narrative.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: The Night House poses as a haunting metaphor for grief alongside horrors that go beyond the expected.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: Those who love their horror served up in heaps of violence and bloodletting may find themselves a bit underwhelmed, if not totally frustrated. However, mystery lovers or those who dig a mesmerizing slow burn will have plenty to be entertained by.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall grounds the ever-shifting film as it transforms from what seems like a straightforward ghost story into something murkier, more troubling and thoroughly unshakeable.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall's powerhouse performance carries this so-so effort across the finish line.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: A well-crafted, mysterious ghost story that manages to keep an audience of 21st-century horror fans entertained. This is not an easy feat.
reviews.author: Rihaana Stark

reviews.text: This is above-average studio horror, genuinely scary with a terrific central performance.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Whatever small contrivances or inconsistencies might dwell in The Night House's story of a husband's secrets and the home they dwell within, they melt away as soon as the camera cuts to the face of its star.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: This one has style at least and Hall is great as a woman in crisis.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Hall... makes terror all the more real because she refuses to yield to it.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Sneaking up behind someone and kicking their ears in the balls does not a master of suspense make.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Intense and well-made, yet the narrative becomes tangled up in itself.
reviews.author: Marina Ashioti

reviews.text: Although let down by muddled plotting, The Night House is a low-key, well-made thoughtful horror flick, excellently played by Rebecca Hall.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Once it loses the horror, the movie can't quite figure out how to combine the power of an expert performance with a muddled and confusing tale about grief, what we leave behind, and depression.
reviews.author: Yolanda Machado

reviews.text: The Night House joins the ranks of many modern horror films that look really damned good but make little sense.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: Hall strives to carry The Night House on her more-than-capable shoulders, but she can't quite compensate for the moments when the movie is outright silly or, worse, boring.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Holds one's interest over most of its overlong running-time, but in the end comes across as murky and unsatisfying.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Although there are number of good scares and a compelling character study at its center, the film leaves us with a disaffected feeling.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: The film features a solid number of thrills, but it never relies on jump scares. Rebecca Hall absolutely nails it, and this subtle yet emotional story does its job.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: The Night House is scary, well-acted, stylish, and gestures toward profundity. Go see it in a theater so you can share the scares.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The ending may disappoint those looking for more definitive answers, but is no less powerful as a meditation on what it takes to move on and live when all you want to do is lie down and join the one you lost.
reviews.author: Mark Cassidy

reviews.text: There is more empathy and depth than the genre typically requires.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: The film is replete with emotional explorations of grief and mental health; it also thoroughly terrifies through sound, visuals, and a proper buildup.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: It's elegantly filmed and well constructed, building to a haunting climatic sequence that could sear your eyeballs.
reviews.author: Chandler Levack

reviews.text: A bubbling, unnerving, flat-out creepy vibe flows throughout, but Bruckner never tips his hand.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Ambiguity lurks in the shadows and there's a doubling up and a doubling down.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Actress Rebecca Hall is the reason to see "The Night House," but the ending is a reason to forget it.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: The Night House [is] a superbly layered slice of dread right up until its final moments.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: [T]here is a wonderful, dark creative spark in its approach that is deeply unsettling and lingers in your brain long after the house lights have gone up.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: It's a disquieting experience, but some of the cheap twists rob it of the gravitas deserved for the complex themes it investigates.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: Bruckner doesn't just depend on Hall's performance but meets it with a mesmerizing visual style that doesn't just leave foreboding voids around her. Instead, it's an active use of empty space, constructing absences that have their own meaning.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: This film about the secrets we all keep, & how those secrets - both inside and outside our control - eventually haunt us. My admiration, nay love, continues for Rebecca Hall.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The film upends the clichés that practically define the ghost story in surprising and intriguing ways.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Bruckner creates shivers, not an easy task when so many horror movies already have taken up residence in similar domains, homes that are presumed to be comforting and safe.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: [David Bruckner], Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski successfully tie in the seemingly obscure references to mazes to create an elaborate maze of this film.
reviews.author: Neely Swanson

reviews.text: 'The Night House' is a tempered approach to horror that's never reliant on jump scares and yet remains so enthrallingly devastating as Rebecca Hall navigates the murkiest depths of mental health as a horror metaphor.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall owns every moment in this psychological thriller and had me looking over my shoulder in the parking lot.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall's performance as a grief-stricken, haunted widow grounds and enhances director David Bruckner's ominous and striking horror feature.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Any problems with the movie are countered by the fact that Hall is just so good at selling its strange concept.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: It's a fun flick and some may still be drawn into The Night House's mystery, but the film-and everyone at the heart of its conception-have Hall to thank for that.
reviews.author: Lex Briscuso

reviews.text: It goes very supernatural indeed. Almost silly in fact. But Hall remains a trouper to the climax, caked by now in free-flowing snot and tears. She smooths over all cracks. She'll carry you through.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: The things that go bump in the night are only the beginning of the scares in "The Night House," where what lingers in the mind is far more terrifying.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Nicely reminiscent of such late 1990s mainstream chillers as Stir of Echoes and The Sixth Sense.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Above all else, The Night House is most successful as a showcase for Rebecca Hall's ravishing range as an actress, as she is asked to exhibit nearly every emotion imaginable over the course of the film's 109-minute runtime
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: The Night House is the kind of horror movie that plays tricks on the mind, scaring us constantly with unpredictable occurrences in every room or hallway, freaking the audience out with both the seen and unseen things that go bump in the night.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: [Hall] intensifies what could've been just another woman with a flashlight in a haunted house movie, peering into the beyond.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Hall is onscreen for almost every minute of the movie and she's always interesting.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Unexplained nocturnal scurryings and knockings are nothing new to this genre, but the filmmaking technique on show is solemn, crisp and often nerve-flayingly effective.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Unsettling, scary, sad. But the central mystery left me with questions that I'm not sure make it an entirely satisfying experience. The reason to see this is Rebecca Hall without question.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: "The Night House" is a creative story with gripping visuals and captivating performances.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: [T]he real success of Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski's screenplay is how this story constantly and consistently evolves.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The Night House is a closed loop, a scary movie about 'big ideas' that wall themselves off and stay safely on the screen.
reviews.author: Chris Mello

reviews.text: With top-notch sound design to truly amplify the experience, this is a must-see for horror fans, one of the better genre pics of 2021.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Another first-rate performance by Rebecca Hall. Once you pull back and process what's happening on screen, it's fascinating as the big picture comes together.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Bruckner... doesn't just mindlessly apply the electrodes; even when he jars you to attention, he always seems to be drawing you into something deeper and more atmospheric. He delivers a scare you can sink into.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: It's a quietly intense alternative to generic horror movies that provides its share of scares without the need to splatter the screen with blood and viscera.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The scares land like blows and the eeriness is pervasive in "The Night House," David Bruckner's hyper-focused, unnervingly sure follow-up to his 2018 wilderness frightener, "The Ritual."
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: The movie's stylized dread lingers, a doorway to an upside-down world whose stakes stay (nearly) real enough to make us care.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: All the elements are there, but there's an unresolved quality to The Night House that drains the life from the film and leaves the viewer frustrated.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: The Night House barely scratches the surface of so much more that is festering underneath.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: The need to "say something" has felled many a talented filmmaker and in this case, chalk Bruckner up as another casualty.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: The Night House is a provocative look at grief with a great lead performance but is undone by a drawn-out approach to the story.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: There is a chilling calm to The Night House that veils the horror beneath. Rebecca Hall gives a seasoned and nuanced performance. The scares are never forced, or even front and center, which makes them more effective when they provoke.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: A tremendously unnerving and tense-filled thriller before eventually becomes that pesky houseguest who overstays their welcome.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Like settling for a bowl of cereal of dinner, David Bruckner's "The Night House" left me wanting more.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The plot may be overloaded, but Rebecca Hall makes expressive choices in every scene capable of selling both emotional drama and supernatural encounters
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Smart enough to feel almost plausible, fun enough to have me screaming "Get out of that house!", this one is my kind of thriller, until it isn't.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Intelligent, emotional, and incredibly eerie.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Rebecca Hall is excellent as the tortured wife of a dead husband searching for answers amid what might be a supernatural maelstrom.
reviews.author: Kim Hughes

reviews.text: Increasingly coiled and prone to barely concealed contempt for the people around her, Hall's Beth is difficult to like, but that's the point.
reviews.author: Tim Stevens

reviews.text: We've been down this dark and woodsy path so many times that, no matter how many scares and shock cuts can be squeezed out of this crafty little thriller, this is a tree that's long since been shorn of most of its leaves.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Hall colours in the character with every line reading and eyebrow flicker, so deeply present in each moment she barely needs co-stars.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: Tight direction, intimate thematic depth, and a powerhouse performance from Rebecca Hall .
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: Calling it intriguing is actually selling it short. Warts and all, "The Night House" is, in the truest sense of the word, kind of haunting.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: The Night House might actually appeal even more to fans of drama than those of horror. That's how effective the emotions are here. Rebecca Hall has never been better.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: While it may house a compelling performance by Rebecca Hall, it's built on a flimsy story that crumbles in the final act.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Led by a captivating performance by Rebecca Hall, it's a film that keeps its feet firmly planted on emotional ground while still proving to be a chilling, atmospheric thriller
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Bruckner achieves career-best work here, establishing spookiness and palpable pressure on the lead character, who connects to several brutal realities in this effective chiller.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: A dark, unsettling tale loaded with terrifying shocks at every turn and emotionally effective moments that expertly capture the crippling chaos of grief.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: A few plot points are left dangling at the end...but make no mistake, this one effective frightener, a real summer sleeper.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Director David Bruckner and actress Rebecca Hall turn the haunted house movie into something fresh and new.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Absolute bravura work from Hall, encased in the thoughtful and perfectly executed craftsmanship that Bruckner brings to the horror genre.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: "The Night House" might not be fondly remembered for how quickly it botches the ending-especially when the first two thirds are exceptional-but a slippery premise that features some startling imagery and commendable jump scares isn't the worst legacy.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: While it may not always pay off the tension it builds, the film's story - about a woman seeking closure after her husband's suicide - makes the lingering unknowability of romance feel just as unsettling as any supernatural force.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The destination is a letdown, but the journey there is harrowing and rewarding. Hall's powerful and affecting performance is the biggest reason why.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Ever a terrific actress, Hall is superb as she embodies the sort of anger that is so often synonymous with feelings of loss, while also epitomizing the crushing loneliness that threatens to smother her character.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Fans of the cult novel 'House of Leaves' should be intrigued by potentially supernatural architectural mysteries while fans of star Hall will be rewarded by a carefully calibrated performance tuned to the release of the movie's revelations.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The Night House is a chillingly atmospheric thriller that serves up quite a few heart-thumping scares. Rebecca Hall is tremendous in a highly nuanced and multilayered performance.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Given the chilling mood Bruckner strikes and dark corners he unearths, horror fans will want to spend some time in this "Night House" even if it's not worth a long-term investment.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: There are enough crafty surprises buried within The Night House to just about outweigh the elements that don't work quite as well, mainly because it's all delivered with such fiery conviction by Hall.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: That the movie remains gripping despite the vagaries of its plotting is due largely to Hall's tough characterization...
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: THE NIGHT HOUSE is a horror film of the mind and the heart and a very successful one at that. It holds no easy answers and is very daring for taking that lonely route.
reviews.author: Dolores Quintana

reviews.text: A strong haunted house film, where ghosts and the occult come into play.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Benefits from [David] Bruckner's finely calibrated direction, Elisha Christian's moody cinematography, and Rebecca Hall's utterly committed central performance.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Bruckner told the premiere crowd your reaction will come down to what you find most frightening, "the idea that ghosts exist or the realization that they don't." The statement alone rattled me. Having it on my mind during his movie chilled me to the bone.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Unfortunately, the script by Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski is clunky-in the convoluted nature of its reveals and also in the sometimes-baffling behavior on display.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Marrying grief and the horror genre isn't exactly new territory, but in The Night House, we see it explored in a much different fashion than before, thanks to an effective and thought-provoking script from writers Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: Whether it's because of the script or David Bruckner's so-so direction, its attempts at eschatological dread don't quite stick.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: It's both human and supernatural in its exploration, and this is what horror, in both the universal encapsulation of fear and our own psychological untangling of it, is supposed to do.
reviews.author: Kristy Strouse

reviews.text: Has a few too many issues to land among the best, but it delivers mightily with jumps that terrify and atmosphere that chills to the bone.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: Hall is fantastic, and she plays her character subtly, tinged with an element of dark humor and wit, instead of reaching for the theatrics that people often mistake for grief.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: If you're in the mood for scares, and a fantastic lead to boot, The Night House demands a visit.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: The Night House has a solid trifecta going for it as it's terrifying when it goes for horror, it's emotionally resonant when it goes for drama, and it's captivating when it doles out bread crumbs of mystery.
reviews.author: Ed Travis

reviews.text: An atmospheric thriller with a great performance by Rebecca Hall.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The Night House is a truly unpredictable experience and there's just as much tension and horror in the very earthly discoveries as the supernatural ones.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: Instead of making the story more ominous with its very broody tone, The Night House negotiates both lacking ideas about loss and dull horror execution.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: The scares in The Night House come hard and fast, aided by director David Bruckner's masterful grasp of a dread-filled atmosphere.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: For as hard as it hits, "The Night House" doesn't bruise enough to follow you home. But the movie's soundscape will vibrate around the hollow of your bones for a long time to come.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Missteps aside, The Night House is a solid ghost story enrobed in the exploration of loss and mortality.
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: An anxiety-inducing, bone-chilling take on the traditional ghost story.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: A knack for creepy atmospherics and individual scares goes a long way in the horror genre, and it takes "The Night House" pretty far.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Bruckner is able to perfectly fold the grounding human drama and Hall's exposed-like-a-raw-nerve performance into insanely effective frights, the jump scares amongst the best in the business; disorienting flashbangs that'll throttle you from your seat.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: The elegantly crafted film falls some way short of its grandest ambitions, but still sends you out into the night with a chill in your bones and the hairs stiff on the back of your neck.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: This is the rare movie where we want her to go through that door or down those stairs, even though we know that what she finds will keep us up at night.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: The horror on display here is so powerful, and Hall's work is so strong, that you're bound to come away from The Night House properly haunted.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

synopsis: Reeling from the unexpected death of her husband, Beth (Rebecca Hall) is left alone in the lakeside home he built for her. She tries as best she can to keep it together -- but then nightmares come. Disturbing visions of a presence in the house calling to her, beckoning her with a ghostly allure. Against the advice of her friends, she begins digging into her husband's belongings, yearning for answers. What she finds are secrets both strange and disturbing -- a mystery she's determined to unravel.
